name: Glacier National Park of Canada
policyReason: Leashed dogs are welcome on many trails, except Balu Pass and, in winter, the backcountry.
summary: Leashed dogs are welcome on many trails, except Balu Pass and, in winter, the backcountry.

excerpts.quote: Dogs are welcome on many trails in Mount Revelstoke and Glacier national parks
While dogs are allowed in most areas, some permanent dog restrictions exist, and temporary restrictions may be present in certain areas due to wildlife activity.

dogRules.text: No dogs on the Balu Pass Trail or in the Connaught Creek drainage (Rogers Pass water supply).
Winter (Nov 15 to May 31): no dogs in the backcountry, meaning anywhere beyond the Trans-Canada Highway parking lots.
Dogs are welcome in Snowforest, Illecillewaet and Loop Brook campgrounds, on leash; store pet food in your vehicle or a bear locker.
Leave your dog at home for the backcountry, or keep it leashed.
